acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Trolls family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Scarlord, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Scar-Shed Bog Bastion (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A bloated mass of overlapping regrowth with bark-hard scar plating across the chest, mismatched limbs of different sizes, and visible wet layers beneath plates ready to shed.

Signature mechanic: Palimpsest Plates: the Scarlord peels one bark-hard chest plate and slams it into the bog. Trolls touching its wet inner face regenerate without exposing their usual bud, while the Scarlord loses armor at the matching chest quadrant. Two adjacent plates can overlap into a covered healing pocket, but striking their bright wet seam collapses both.
battlefieldDuty: Build temporary healing territory by tearing off overlapping chest plates as cover and regrowth beds, then using mismatched limbs to patrol the seams between them.
constructionDimensions: Misgrown anatomy develops pressure-catching tissue: stretched scar membranes between extra limbs, hollow callus vents, rag streamers healed into skin, and vane-like ribs grow from recognizable wounds.

Movement and silhouette become directionally elastic through inflated wound sacs, bowed long arms, flapping membranes, mud streamers, and one-way pressure releases that snap a distorted limb into its attack path.
counterplay: Attack the newly soft chest quadrant, strike the wet overlap before lower forms enter, or force the Scarlord to place plates apart so they cannot form a protected pocket. Affinity signal: One scar membrane stretches translucent and its connected wound sac inflates along the intended direction; puncturing the sac or moving into the still lee collapses the attack.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only wind treatment without scar membranes, vents, and directional elasticity
Glow-only wind treatment without pressure-bearing anatomy or readable airflow
Weightless floating Trolls that abandon long-limbed ground contact
Turbulence that hides active wounds or the still lee
identityInvariants: Tall, stooped, potbellied humanoid silhouette with a small head on a thick neck and disproportionately long arms hanging past the knees.
Bog green, liver-brown, sallow grey, bruise purple, and wet glistening highlights keep living hide distinct from mud and scavenged rags.
Rubbery skin, scar tissue, bark-hard callus, mud, rope, and half-swallowed equipment remain visibly bodily rather than worn as deliberate finery.
Healed-over piercings, embedded bones, lodged weapons, misplaced limbs, stray jaws, and layered scars record prior injury as readable construction history.
Escalation adds accumulated misregrowth rather than simple size: open gashes become knots, alternate organs, defensive scar architecture, and finally a walking archive of incompatible healing.
telegraph: Mismatched arms hook beneath a cracked chest plate, dark fluid beads around its edge, and nearby Trolls turn their open wounds toward the glistening inner surface.
